<issue_description>
Using singe quote as part of JSON object key leads to invalid SQL generation
**Before you file an issue**
- Make sure you specify the "read" dialect eg. `parse_one(sql, read="spark")` - ok
- Make sure you specify the "write" dialect eg. `ast.sql(dialect="duckdb")` - ok
- Check if the issue still exists on main - checked on sqlglot-25.20.2.dev5

**Overview**

When querying inside JSON object in Snowflake and referenced object's key contains `'` character the statements seems to be parsed correctly but when generating SQL the output is not valid (at least for snowflake and postgres dialects). Replacing single `'` in key name with escaped one: `''` resolves at least this case.

Object key can be referenced using `:` notation (e.g. `json_doc:"Customer's department"`) or using `get_path` function (`GET_PATH(PARSE_JSON(doc), '"Customer''s department"')`) - the result is the same.

**Fully reproducible code snippet**

```python
import sqlglot
sql_text = """select parse_json(doc):"Customer's department"::string as "dept" from json_tbl"""
print(sqlglot.parse_one(sql_text, dialect="snowflake").sql(dialect="snowflake"))
# SELECT CAST(GET_PATH(PARSE_JSON(doc), '["Customer's department"]') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl

print(sqlglot.parse_one(sql_text, dialect="snowflake").sql(dialect="postgres"))
# SELECT CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_PATH(CAST(doc AS JSON), 'Customer's department') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl
```
Expecting output for Snowflake to be 
```sql
SELECT CAST(GET_PATH(PARSE_JSON(doc), '["Customer''s department"]') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl;
-- or
SELECT CAST(GET_PATH(PARSE_JSON(doc), '"Customer''s department"') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl;
-- or, if not using GET_PATH function the original name without escaped quote can be used
SELECT CAST(PARSE_JSON(doc):"Customer's department" AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl;
```
And for PostgreSQL
```sql
SELECT CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_PATH(CAST(doc AS JSON), 'Customer''s department') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl;
```

To test query with postgres:
```sql
create table json_tbl(doc jsonb);
insert into json_tbl values('{"Customer''s department": "Department A"}');

-- invalid query:
SELECT CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_PATH(CAST(doc AS JSON), 'Customer's department') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl;
/*
ERROR:  syntax error at or near "s"
LINE 1: ...ST(JSON_EXTRACT_PATH(CAST(doc AS JSON), 'Customer's departme...
                                                             ^ 

SQL state: 42601
Character: 60
*/
-- valid query:
SELECT CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_PATH(CAST(doc AS JSON), 'Customer''s department') AS TEXT) AS "dept" FROM json_tbl;
```


**Official Documentation**
Please include links to official SQL documentation related to your issue.
- [Snowflake: Double quoted identifiers](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/identifiers-syntax#double-quoted-identifiers)
- [Snowflake: Single-quoted string constants](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/data-types-text#label-single-quoted-string-constants)

**Problem Summary**: When parsing SQL queries containing JSON object keys with single quotes (like `"Customer's department"`), sqlglot correctly parses the input but fails to properly escape single quotes when generating SQL output for Snowflake and Postgres dialects.

**Technical Details**:
- Method names involved: `parse_one()`, `.sql()` method
- Error pattern: Unescaped single quotes in generated JSON path strings
- File context: JSON path expression handling in dialect conversion
- Key issue: `GET_PATH(PARSE_JSON(doc), '["Customer's department"]')` has unescaped quote

**Clear Problem Statement**: 
The SQL generation logic doesn't properly escape single quotes within JSON path strings when converting AST back to SQL for different database dialects.

**Reproduction Steps**:
1. Parse: `select parse_json(doc):"Customer's department"::string as "dept" from json_tbl` with Snowflake dialect
2. Generate SQL with Snowflake or Postgres dialect
3. Observe incorrectly escaped single quotes in JSON path

**Best Practices for Fix**:
- Handle dialect-specific escaping rules
- Focus on JSON path string generation
- Maintain backward compatibility
- Test with various quote scenarios

     3	SQLGlot is a no-dependency SQL parser, transpiler, optimizer, and engine. It can be used to format SQL or translate between [21 different dialects](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/main/sqlglot/dialects/__init__.py) like [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/), [Presto](https://prestodb.io/) / [Trino](https://trino.io/), [Spark](https://spark.apache.org/) / [Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/), and [BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/). It aims to read a wide variety of SQL inputs and output syntactically and semantically correct SQL in the targeted dialects.
     4	
     5	It is a very comprehensive generic SQL parser with a robust [test suite](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/main/tests/). It is also quite [performant](#benchmarks), while being written purely in Python.
     6	
     7	You can easily [customize](#custom-dialects) the parser, [analyze](#metadata) queries, traverse expression trees, and programmatically [build](#build-and-modify-sql) SQL.
     8	
     9	Syntax [errors](#parser-errors) are highlighted and dialect incompatibilities can warn or raise depending on configurations. However, SQLGlot does not aim to be a SQL validator, so it may fail to detect certain syntax errors.
    10
